N-1.9-A.skill: decide whether limits of sums and products exist from one-sided limits read off two described graphs, without using the function values at the point.

N-1.9-B.skill: recognize that a table of values on a special sequence of inputs can mislead, and use an algebraic or graphical description to decide whether a limit exists.

N-1.10-A.skill: classify a discontinuity from one-sided limits of an inverse-trigonometric expression and reject an argument that confuses f(a) with a limit.

N-1.10-B.skill: read a described graph, sort each special x-value into removable, jump, infinite, or continuous, and count correctly without counting the continuous point.

N-1.11-A.skill: apply the three-part definition of continuity to a piecewise function with exponential and logarithmic pieces, evaluating ln 1 and e⁰ correctly and including f(2).

N-1.11-B.skill: translate the definition of continuity into limit notation, separating conditions that only compare the two sides from the condition that links the limit to the function value.

N-1.12-A.skill: find the largest set of continuity for a quotient of inverse-trigonometric and logarithmic expressions by intersecting domain restrictions and removing zeros of the denominator.

N-1.12-B.skill: make a three-piece function continuous on all real numbers by matching both junction points, tracking how ln(1) and e⁰ remove or keep parameters.

N-1.13-A.skill: find the value that removes a discontinuity when the limit requires a double-angle identity and the special trigonometric limit sin(u)/u → 1.

N-1.13-B.skill: first find the constant that makes a radical quotient a 0/0 form, then rationalize and find the value that removes the discontinuity.

N-1.14-A.skill: locate vertical asymptotes of a quotient with a logarithm, rejecting a false asymptote at the edge of the domain, and determine the sign of the one-sided infinite limits.

N-1.14-B.skill: evaluate a difference of two unbounded terms by combining them first, deciding which term dominates instead of treating ∞ − ∞ as a number.

N-1.15-A.skill: evaluate an ∞ − ∞ limit of a radical difference by multiplying by the conjugate, then divide through by the dominant power.

N-1.15-B.skill: find horizontal asymptotes at both ends of an exponential rational function, recognizing which exponential dominates as x → ∞ and as x → −∞.

N-1.16-A.skill: count the zeros that the Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees from a table by checking each subinterval for a sign change, rather than comparing endpoints or counting every interval.

N-1.16-B.skill: choose the interval on which the Intermediate Value Theorem actually applies to an equation, checking both continuity and a sign change of the rewritten function.
